chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When you intend to slaughter the Aqeeqa, you say: 'O my people! I am clear of what you associate (with Allah). I have turned my face toward Him who originated the heavens and the earth, upright and submitting, and I am not of the polytheists. Surely my prayer and my sacrifice and my life and my death are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. There is no associate for Him, and with that I am commanded, and I am of the Muslims.'

O Allah, from You and for You, in the Name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and accept from so-and-so, son of so-and-so' – and name the newborn with his name, then slaughter.

key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةَ: Aqeeqa, the sacrifice slaughtered for a newborn child
key_terms.حَنِيفاً: Upright, monotheistic, turning away from polytheism
key_terms.فُلَانِ بْنِ فُلَانٍ: So-and-so son of so-and-so, a placeholder for naming the specific individual

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended recitations and steps for performing the Aqeeqa sacrifice in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the specific recitations for the Aqeeqa sacrifice, integrating the 'Qunut' verses (6:162-163) with the declaration of monotheism from Surah Al-An'am to emphasize the child's dedication to Allah. It highlights the Shia practice of invoking blessings upon the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt during the ritual, linking the physical act of sacrifice with spiritual purification and acceptance by the Divine.
